input: nums is a plain list of integers in increasing order; target is an integer. Preconditions are not checked at runtime.
return: An integer in [0, n]: the first index whose value is at least target, or n. Empty input returns 0. If duplicate values are supplied, the first matching position is returned as an explicit extension, not a predecessor-equivalence claim.
mutation_aliasing: No input writes, sorting or copies. The result is an integer. The Solution instance retains no state.
numeric: The paired contract restricts values and target to integers in [-9007199254740991, 9007199254740991]. Python integer comparisons and index arithmetic are exact. No target arithmetic is used.
complexity: O(log(n + 1)) time and O(1) auxiliary space under constant-cost indexing and machine-word comparisons.

helpers.name: lower_bound
helpers.contract: Returns the first index whose value is at least target, or n; searches [left, right).
helpers.cost: One call, O(log(n + 1)) time and O(1) space. Its complete identical definition is included in each of the three search candidates.
